sources.citation: Daniels, Don (2015). Sirva grammar sketch. In A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram: Phonology, Lexicon, and Morphosyntax. Santa Barbara: University of California at Santa Barbara. pp. 658-765.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Sirva is not in the catalog and has no existing stress statements; this, its only grammatical description, is silent on word stress, so the catalog gap stands. The author himself flags Sogeram stress systems as unresearched (p. 72).
Nothing; vowel table copied from Daniels 2015: 96.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don Roger. 2015. A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram: Phonology, Lexicon, and Morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. 1127 pp. Sirva: sec. 2.3.6 'Sirva Innovations' pp. 96-98; Appendix 3 'Sirva Grammar Sketch' pp. 658-765, phonology sec. 3.2-3.2.1 pp. 662-667. eScholarship qt1kj4174g.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Sirva: sec. 3.2 gives consonant/vowel inventories, affricate allophony, lenition, prenasalization, diphthongs, /ɨ/ phonemic status, marginal long /i/, and morphophonemics (vowel elision, coronal reduction, labial merging); no word on stress, accent or tone. Only stress remark in the whole work is p. 71 (Mand chapter): 'Further research into the stress systems of the Sogeram languages might reveal a consistent pattern.'
